title: Implement the conditional-radius selector with rational cuts and controlled bit growth
statement: Given NUMERIC B>=1 and a theta-star of norm<=B with original mean-gradient norm<=epsilon/32, set tau=epsilon/(32B),G=F+tau||theta||^2/2. Its optimizer has norm<3B. On[-4B-1,4B+1]^d compute rational Hessian upper M>=1 with logM=poly_R(L+B); let D=8dB+1,g0=epsilon/16,delta=min(g0/4,tau*g0^2/(16M^2 D)),mu=tau*g0^2/(8M^2),r0=min(B/2,mu/[2(MD+1)]). Maintain rational K initially[-4B,4B]^d. Enumerate vertices, choose a maximum-volume vertex simplex, query its centroid using a fixed dyadic gradient approximation of error<=delta. A small approximate gradient gives original coordinate error<=epsilon/4; otherwise its central cut retains the radius-r0 optimizer ball. Absolute barycentric coordinates<=1 give volK<=2^d d! volSimplex; a centered symmetrized1/d simplex gives removal fraction alpha_d=1/[2^(d+1)d!d^d]. Thus O_R(log(B/r0)) cuts suffice. Fixed dyadic integer normals have polynomial bit height Q; common facet-offset denominator grows only O_R(Q) bits per cut through fixed-size determinants, avoiding exponential nested rational growth. Paid DDB1 moment/exp calls and log-rounding<=epsilon/(16dM) return ordinary positive rational lambda. Total work/memory/output poly_R(L+B), B NUMERIC. This completes selection CONDITIONAL on a supplied radius, not a global polynomial-radius theorem.
